meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's essay. Who decided on the zero, and before or after anyone spoke to him?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. And before you entered it, did anyone speak to Owen?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
Writing it elsewhere and pasting it in leaves exactly that history. Turn the screen so I can read the entries myself. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Pull it up. I'm writing the times down as you read them.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote plays from memory all the time. Run the search while I watch.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
An outline is a plan, and a student can change his argument after he's thought about it more. Put both pages in front of me.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
A seventeen-year-old put on the spot by his teacher will say "like, being stuck." Did you tell him what the questions were for, or that a mark depended on his answers?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes under a clock isn't a weekend with the play open. And you skipped my question about November 2.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says not to use it alone. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. And you still haven't answered me about November 2.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4. I want it in writing, private, not in front of his class. And I haven't seen the version history or the search on your screen yet.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Not until I've read the version history and watched the search myself. Turn the screen. After that, I want a date for the rewrite and the new mark in before December first.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Screen first. The version history, then the search. I'll give you a day after I've read them.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. Nothing is agreed until I've seen the version history with my own eyes. Turn the screen.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Ten minutes. The version history on your screen, the search for that line, and the terms in your email tonight. Start with the screen.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the version history and the search for the quotation shown to me on your screen, and the terms in writing: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replacing the zero, nothing on Owen's record, and a date that puts the new mark in before December 1. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She moved from opening to fallback, with the zero withdrawn and nothing on his record still her aim, and she accepted that 4.4 would meet her demand, but she agreed to nothing because you never turned your screen to her; she still wants to see the history and the search, plus the terms in writing and a rewrite date before December 1, and the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite, nothing on his record) was on the table but not closed, with her time not yet run out.
What moved her: You put exact times from the version history in front of her and told her she could check them herself, because a dated document she can verify is the one thing she weighs.
What cost ground: You asked her to confirm terms before she had seen anything on your screen, because that kept her demanding evidence instead of closing the deal.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence of a blank document at 11:31 PM on October 28 filling with text by 11:58 came close to that kind of night, which is why she went to procedure, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you first offered the version history, turn the screen to her at once and let her read the entries before you mention the rewrite.
